ICYMI: Conference Chairwoman McClain Attends Michigan Farm Bureau Dinner on the Farm | Press Releases | Congresswoman Lisa McClain Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Press Releases Print ICYMI: Conference Chairwoman McClain Attends Michigan Farm Bureau Dinner on the Farm August 27 , 2026 MICHIGAN   –  House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) this week joined the annual Michigan Farm Bureau Dinner on the Farm at Zwerk & Sons Farms to highlight the benefits of the Working Families Tax Cuts for Michigan farmers and to discuss ongoing work to pass a long-term Farm Bill. Attendees included House Agriculture Committee Vice Chairman Austin Scott (R-Ga.); Matt Frostic of Frostic Farms and the National Corn Growers Association; Mike Noll of Noll Farms and Michigan Farm Bureau; and Michigan Farm Bureau President Ben LaCross.  “It was a rewarding evening of honest discussions with Michigan farmers who work tirelessly every day to feed our families and boost our economy. Washington should support their efforts by making their work easier,”  Chairwoman McClain said . “I fought to deliver meaningful wins for our farmers through the Working Families Tax Cuts, and I will continue pushing to reduce input costs, cut through excessive red tape, and get a long-term Farm Bill across the finish line to bring much-needed relief to our agricultural community.” “I want to thank Chairwoman McClain for inviting me to join her at Dinner on the Farm and giving me the opportunity to hear from Michigan’s farmers. Chairwoman McClain Holds Field Hearing on Supporting Servicemembers Serving on School Boards | Press Releases | Congresswoman Lisa McClain Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Press Releases Print Chairwoman McClain Holds Field Hearing on Supporting Servicemembers Serving on School Boards August 25 , 2026 MICHIGAN - House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) and Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) today held a field hearing at Richmond City Hall titled Deployed, Not Disqualified: Defending Servicemembers in Our Schools. The hearing examined how schools, communities, and government can better support servicemembers participating in their local school systems. Master Sergeant Raymond Stier, an elected member of the Richmond Board of Education, faced pressure from fellow board members to resign while deployed overseas, despite attending board meetings virtually when he could. Some board members later criticized his absence as a "disservice". The hearing featured testimony from Amy Stier, Master Sergeant Stier's wife; Colonel Chris Neeley, superintendent of the South Carolina Public Charter School District; and Jonathan Butcher, an education policy expert at the Heritage Foundation. "Richmond knew exactly whom it elected, a man with three decades in uniform," Chairwoman McClain said . "After being deployed to the Middle East, despite significant time zone differences, Master Sergeant Stier continued to serve his community virtually. He kept his oath to his country and to this community and took fire for both. The board members should be ashamed of forcing a servicemember to choose between serving their country and their community." ICYMI: Chairwoman McClain Hosts Oakland County Job Fair for Michigan Job Seekers | Press Releases | Congresswoman Lisa McClain Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Press Releases Print ICYMI: Chairwoman McClain Hosts Oakland County Job Fair for Michigan Job Seekers August 15 , 2026 MICHIGAN—  On Thursday, August 13, House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.), in partnership with Michigan Works, hosted the inaugural Southeast Michigan Job Fair at Oakland University. The event connected employers with job seekers from across the region. Joined by the Small Business Administration (SBA) Deputy Administrator Bill Briggs, the event connected nearly 700 hardworking Michiganders with 100 businesses. Participating companies included General Motors, McLaren Health Care, and ZF Axle Drives, each offering a wide range of positions, from entry-level to skilled roles. “Events like the Southeast Michigan Job Fair are critical to connecting job creators with hardworking Michigan job seekers,”  Chairwoman McClain said . “Through the Working Families Tax Cuts, America is getting back to work, and employers and employees alike are experiencing much-needed relief, helping fulfill the America First agenda by expanding opportunities to quality, high-paying jobs.” "The Southeast Michigan Job Fair was a great example of what we can accomplish when we come together as a region. We connected employers who are hiring with job seekers looking for their next opportunity. In such a digital world, there’s something especially impactful about bringing people together face-to-face and creating a real sense of community,”  said Michigan Works! Macomb/St. Clair. House Passes Chairwoman McClain’s Common Cents Act to End Wasteful Penny Production | Press Releases | Congresswoman Lisa McClain Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Press Releases Print House Passes Chairwoman McClain’s Common Cents Act to End Wasteful Penny Production July 14 , 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the House of Representatives passed House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain's (R-Mich.) Common Cents Act. This legislation permanently ends production of the penny for general circulation. “Washington has a spending problem, and it shows up in places big and small,” Chairwoman McClain said. “If the federal government is spending nearly four cents to make a penny worth one cent, something is broken. House Republicans are proving that common sense still has a place in government by cutting waste and protecting taxpayer dollars.” President Trump directed the Treasury Department to end production of new pennies after the cost of producing each coin reached 3.69 cents. The Common Cents Act permanently codifies that policy while allowing the U.S. Mint to continue producing limited collectible pennies. Existing pennies may still be used for all cash transactions, and businesses may continue providing exact change. Payments made electronically, by credit card, check, gift card, or other non-cash methods are still charged to the exact cent. The legislation establishes a national framework for cash transactions when exact change is unavailable. It also authorizes the Treasury Department to use a lower-cost composition for the nickel if testing demonstrates it reduces production costs without significantly affecting coin-operated machines.
